findings.title: [P1] Pass branch names without invoking a shell
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell metacharacters, `exec` interprets them as commands. For example, `showBranch("main; malicious-command")` executes the additional command with the current process’s privileges. The previous `execFile` implementation passed the branch as a literal Git argument.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the Git process
findings.body: On Windows, `exec` returns the shell process rather than the spawned Git process. Calling `kill()` on the returned handle can terminate `cmd.exe` while leaving Git running and its inherited pipes open. The previous `execFile` implementation returned the directly spawned Git process.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the actual Git process
findings.body:
`exec()` returns the shell process rather than `git` on Windows. If a caller invokes `showBranch(...).kill()` during a long-running `git show`, only `cmd.exe` is terminated; the Git child can continue consuming resources, keep inherited pipes open, and delay stream closure. `execFile()` previously allowed callers to terminate Git directly.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Avoid interpolating the branch into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell, so an attacker-controlled branch such as `HEAD; arbitrary-command` on POSIX (or `HEAD & arbitrary-command` on Windows) executes additional commands with the process’s privileges. The previous `execFile` call passed the branch as a literal argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass branch names without invoking a shell
findings.body:
`exec` interpolates `branch` into a shell command, allowing arbitrary command execution when the exported function receives attacker-controlled input. For example, `showBranch("main; malicious-command")` executes both commands; the prior `execFile` implementation treated the value solely as a Git argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Preserve argv-based execution to prevent unowned subprocesses
findings.body:
`exec` shell-parses `branch`. On POSIX, input such as `HEAD;nohup yes>/dev/null 2>&1&` launches an unbounded CPU-consuming process that outlives the returned `ChildProcess`, so callers cannot clean it up through that handle. Any caller able to influence `branch` can cause persistent resource exhaustion.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
